sections.heading: Section 1: Degrees and the Handshaking Lemma

questions.q: What does the Handshaking Lemma state for any undirected graph with $V$ vertices and $E$ edges?
choices: The sum of the degrees of all vertices equals twice the number of edges: $\sum \deg(v) = 2E$
The sum of the degrees equals $E$
The number of vertices with odd degree is always odd
Every vertex must have degree at least 2
questions.answer: Because every edge connects two endpoints, each edge contributes exactly 2 to the sum of the degrees of the vertices: $\sum \deg(v) = 2E$.

questions.q: A graph has $6$ vertices, each having degree $3$. How many edges does the graph have?
Why can a graph never have an odd number of vertices of odd degree?
choices: Because $\sum \deg(v) = 2E$ is always even, the sum of odd degrees must be even, forcing an even count of odd vertices
Because edges cannot cross each other
By Euler's formula $V - E + F = 2$
Because every vertex must have at least one adjacent edge
questions.answer: The total sum of degrees is even ($2E$). The sum of even degrees is even, so the sum of the odd degrees must also be even, which requires an even number of odd terms.

sections.heading: Section 2: Eulerian and Hamiltonian Paths and Circuits

questions.q: What condition is both necessary and sufficient for a connected graph to contain an Eulerian circuit (a closed trail visiting every edge exactly once)?
choices: Every vertex has an even degree
Exactly two vertices have odd degree
The graph contains no cycles
The graph is a complete bipartite graph
questions.answer: Euler proved that a connected graph has an Eulerian circuit if and only if all vertices have even degree.

questions.q: If a connected graph has exactly two vertices of odd degree, what type of Eulerian walk does it contain?
choices: An Eulerian trail (open path visiting every edge once) that starts at one odd vertex and ends at the other
An Eulerian circuit returning to the start
No Eulerian trail or circuit can exist
A Hamiltonian cycle
questions.answer: Euler's theorem guarantees an open Eulerian trail if and only if exactly two vertices have odd degree; the trail must start at one odd vertex and terminate at the other.

questions.q: What is the difference between an Eulerian circuit and a Hamiltonian cycle?
choices: An Eulerian circuit visits every edge once; a Hamiltonian cycle visits every vertex once
An Eulerian circuit visits every vertex once; a Hamiltonian cycle visits every edge once
They are identical concepts in graph theory
Hamiltonian cycles apply only to directed trees
questions.answer: Eulerian paths/circuits pertain to visiting every edge, while Hamiltonian paths/cycles pertain to visiting every vertex.

questions.q: In a connected weighted graph with $V$ vertices, how many edges does any spanning tree contain?
questions.answer: Any tree on $V$ vertices is minimally connected and contains no cycles, having precisely $V - 1$ edges.

questions.q: How does Kruskal's algorithm select edges to construct a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST)?
choices: Sorts all edges by weight and greedily adds the smallest available edge that does not create a cycle
Grows a single tree by continuously adding the closest vertex to the current tree
Removes the largest cycle edges one by one until only a tree remains
Visits vertices in alphabetical order
questions.answer: Kruskal's algorithm is an edge-based greedy algorithm that adds edges in order of increasing weight, rejecting any edge that completes a cycle.

questions.q: How does Prim's algorithm differ conceptually from Kruskal's algorithm?
choices: Prim grows a single connected tree from an arbitrary starting vertex, whereas Kruskal maintains a forest of components until unified
Prim works only on unweighted graphs
Kruskal finds the longest path rather than minimum tree
Prim can only be applied to planar graphs
questions.answer: Prim's algorithm builds a single growing connected tree vertex by vertex, whereas Kruskal's algorithm connects disjoint components across the whole graph.

sections.heading: Section 4: Shortest Paths and Dijkstra's Algorithm

questions.q: What is the purpose of Dijkstra's algorithm?
choices: To find the shortest paths from a single source vertex to all other vertices in a network with non-negative edge weights
To find a minimum spanning tree
To determine if a graph has an Eulerian circuit
To find the maximum flow through a network
questions.answer: Dijkstra's algorithm is the standard greedy algorithm for computing single-source shortest paths on graphs with non-negative edge weights.

questions.q: Why does Dijkstra's algorithm fail if a network contains negative edge weights?
choices: A greedy choice once finalized could be improved later by a negative edge, invalidating the optimality assumption
Distances cannot be negative by definition
The algorithm enters an infinite cycle immediately
Square roots of negative weights cannot be computed
questions.answer: Dijkstra's greedy assumption assumes that once a vertex distance is finalized, no shorter path to it exists; negative edges violate this monotonic property.

questions.q: In a planar graph, if $V = 6$ and $E = 9$, how many faces $F$ does the graph enclose according to Euler's formula $V - E + F = 2$?
questions.answer: By Euler's planar formula $V - E + F = 2$: $6 - 9 + F = 2 \Rightarrow -3 + F = 2 \Rightarrow F = 5$.
